newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two hurt in bombing of Corsica apartment block.
newsitem.headline: Two hurt in bombing of Corsica apartment block.

text.p: Two women were taken to hospital suffering from shock after an overnight bombing attack on an apartment block in Ajaccio on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, police said on Sunday.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.

Bombings are common on the island where separatist groups have waged a two-decade-long campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France, but police said they were puzzled by the latest blast because it differed from most separatist attacks.
Its target was a residence and a stick of dynamite went off by the door of each of 17 ground-floor flats, while separatists typically target uninhabited buildings and use a single charge.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing has stepped up its guerrilla campaign since the detention on December 16 of Francois Santoni, head of the Conculta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing.
Santoni faces charges of attempted extortion and arms violations.

The FLNC on Saturday claimed responsibility for the Friday night bombing of departmental agricultural offices in the town of Pietrabugno and a rocket attack a day earlier on the law courts building in Bastia, northern Corsica.
